steps.notes: Prompt-compliant Busing-Levy B (x*//a*, z*//(a* x b*)) fails ALL 3 tests; target is bit-exactly inv(A) with A = direct-lattice column matrix (a//x, b in xy plane). See D7 finding.
Literal reading (k=1/lambda, lab frame +x beam / +z up, x_det//-y, y_det//-z, Q=k_s-k_i, (3,1) shape) passes all 3 tests.

Passes with theta = z*z_s (z as passed, 0-based per docstring), back-rotation R_y(+theta) for crystal rotated about -y, t2 = t3 x t1, elements (3,1). Docstring says 'phi rotation' where everything else says theta (minor).
U = T_g @ T_c.T passes all 3 tests; targets are orthogonal matrices as documented.

hkl = inv(U@B) @ R_y(z*z_s) @ Q passes all 4 tests; targets ~ integer hkl consistent with physics. Background text has corrupted step references and an undefined 'G' matrix, but the closed-form summary formula makes it solvable.

findings.evidence: Prompt: 'Write down the matrix B that transforms (h,k,l) coordinates from the reciprocal lattice system to (q_x,q_y,q_z) coordinates in the right-handed Cartesian system ... with x^*//a^* and z^*//(a^* x b^*)' and 'convention a_i . b_j = delta_ij'. The unique matrix satisfying this is the Busing-Levy matrix B_BL = [[a*, b*cos(g*), c*cos(b*)],[0, b*sin(g*), -c*sin(b*)cos(alpha)],[0,0,1/c]]. steptest: B_BL FAILS all 3 tests (official joint: FAIL); worst |diff|/(atol+rtol|tgt|) = 174 (test 0), 174 (test 1), 20441 (test 2, gamma=120.1). The h5 target is instead bit-exactly inv(A) (max|diff| = 0.0 on tests 0-1, 1.8e-20 on test 2), where A is the DIRECT-lattice column matrix embedded with a//x and b in the x-y plane, i.e. the reciprocal primitive vectors appear as ROWS of the target in a direct-lattice-aligned frame. This violates the stated frame (target column 0 = (1/a,0,0), not (a*,0,0); target row 0 = a* has nonzero y,z components, so neither columns nor rows put a* along x). Worse, the target is not metric-correct as an hkl->q map: target.T @ target != G* (reciprocal metric), while target @ target.T == G*, proving it is the TRANSPOSE of a valid mapping (rows/columns slip in the reference). A solver returning inv(A) passes officially (verified: review/work/61/impl_refconv.py PASS).
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate the 61.1 h5 targets with the Busing-Levy matrix that the prompt actually specifies (upper-triangular, B[0,0]=a*, B[2,2]=1/c, columns = reciprocal vectors in the x//a*, z//(a* x b*) frame). Alternatively rewrite the prompt to ask for inv(A) explicitly ('matrix whose rows are the reciprocal primitive vectors, in the Cartesian frame with x//a and b in the x-y plane') - but the current reference object is also physically dubious as a transform (transposed), so fixing the target is the better repair.

findings.evidence: Every test of steps 61.3-61.5 uses an ideal cubic cell (a=b=c=5.39097, alpha=beta=gamma=90), for which all B-matrix conventions degenerate to (1/a)*I. Consequently the orientation pipeline never exercises the non-orthogonal machinery that step 61.1 sets up: my Busing-Levy Bmat (which FAILS 61.1's target) passes 61.3, 61.4 and 61.5, and so would the reference's transposed inv(A); any B wrong by an arbitrary rotation or transpose also passes (U = T_g T_c^T absorbs rotations, and transpose errors vanish for cubic cells). A metric-wrong Bmat is thus undetectable downstream.
findings.suggested_fix: Add at least one 61.5 (or 61.3) test case with a triclinic/hexagonal cell (e.g. the gamma=120.1 parameters already used in 61.1) so the B convention is actually constrained by the integrated pipeline.

findings.evidence: Docstring: 'z_s: step size in the \phi rotation, float in the unit of degree', but the step prompt describes rotation 'along the -y axis ... characterized by a specific rotation angle theta', and the main problem I/O plus 61.5 call the same parameter 'step size in the theta rotation'. Same physical quantity, inconsistent symbol.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename to 'step size in the theta rotation' in the 61.3 docstring.

findings.evidence: Background text is corrupted: 'Employ step to calculate the momentum transfer Q' and '2. Utilize G matrix obtained from step to rotate Q back' have missing step numbers (a numbered list lost its references), and the goniometer matrix G is never formally defined anywhere in the problem. The docstring also contains a literal-tab corruption ('step size in the 	heta rotation' renders as 'the heta rotation') and describes the return as 'q: 3x1 orthogonal matrix' - 'orthogonal' is meaningless for a 3x1 vector and the output is actually (h,k,l). All of this is recoverable: the closed-form summary '(h,k,l) = (UB)^{-1} G^{-1} Q' plus step 61.3's back-rotation construction make G inferable as R_{-y}(theta_z), and my literal implementation passed all 4 tests.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the step references ('Employ step 2 ...', 'G matrix obtained from the frame rotation of step 3'), define G = R_y(-theta_z) (rotation of the diffractometer at frame z, theta_z = z*z_s about -y), fix the \theta escaping, and change the output doc to 'q: (h,k,l) indices, 3x1 array, float'.

overall_assessment: Steps 61.2-61.5 are solvable, deterministic, well-targeted and pass with a literal expert reading (theta = z*z_s with 0-based frames, back-rotation R_y(+theta), U = T_g T_c^T, hkl = (UB)^{-1}G^{-1}Q). Step 61.1 is a hard false negative: the frozen target encodes inv(A) - the transposed reciprocal-vector matrix in a DIRECT-lattice-aligned frame - while the prompt unambiguously specifies the Busing-Levy convention (x*//a*, z*//(a* x b*)); every prompt-compliant solution fails all three tests by 2-4 orders of magnitude beyond tolerance. Because steps 3-5 only test cubic cells, this inconsistency is invisible downstream, so the rest of the problem scores fairly, but 61.1 as-is mis-scores every competent solver.
